questions.stem: Why can most plants not use nitrogen gas (N2) directly from the atmosphere?

options.text: Because nitrogen gas is too heavy to be absorbed by leaves
Because plants can only absorb nitrogen through their flowers
Because nitrogen gas is very unreactive and must first be converted into soluble compounds
Because there is not enough nitrogen in the atmosphere

questions.explanation: Nitrogen gas (N2) has a very strong triple bond between its atoms, making it unreactive. Plants can only absorb nitrogen in soluble forms such as nitrates from the soil, so nitrogen must first be fixed into usable compounds by bacteria or lightning.
